brief: Beam is a high-throughput parallel downloader written in Go with zero dependencies. Its frontend follows a distinct neo-brutalist / retro-editorial chassis: solid color palettes (zero gradients), tactile rivets, 2px solid dark ink borders, hard shadow offsets, and a Windows XP file-transfer metaphor.
criteria: Success: immediate recognition at 16 px favicon, matches the frontend chassis aesthetic, works across dark and light cockpit themes, zero gradients.

concepts.name: The Byte-Range B
concepts.idea: A neo-brutalist letterform 'B' sliced into 4 discrete concurrency byte blocks with a forward velocity ray.
rationale: Unambiguous 'B' letterform equity that fits cleanly into 16 px app icons and favicons
Horizontal slice intervals directly express RFC 7233 chunk partitioning
Thick ink outlines and hard drop shadow match the frontend dashboard cards

concepts.name: The Velocity Folder
concepts.idea: A tactile neo-brutalist file folder with a protruding tab and a high-voltage 60° mint lightning beam.
rationale: Direct visual evolution of the dashboard's '.brand-folder-tab' and retro-XP file transfer theme
Tactile rivets and hard shadow create instant mechanical presence
High-voltage Mint bolt provides striking contrast against Butter Yellow flap

concepts.name: The Concurrency Stream
concepts.idea: Four concurrent worker conduits fanning out from a central intake into forward velocity beams.
rationale: Directly visualizes the 4-worker goroutine streaming architecture
Staggered progress bands mirror the live worker telemetry tracks in the UI
Clean 45-degree forward chevrons communicate supersonic network throughput

recommendation: The Velocity Folder (Concept B) — creates an exact 1:1 thematic bridge with the web cockpit's folder tabs while giving Beam an unmistakable, nostalgic, and high-energy brand icon.
